To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
patients with ideomotor aphasia make errors when they imitate meaningless movements with their left hand.
ideomotor apractic patients commit errors when they imitate movements with their left hand and that these errors are due to a conceptual deficit.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the brain organizes the production of movements.
the question of how the brain mediates the imitation of meaningless gestures, and how the brain mediats the control of skilled movement in general.
the question of cerebral dominance for motor function and the nature of the deficits in patients with apractic errors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the left hemisphere has a dominant role for the conceptual representation of movements, and that the right hemisphere may be dominant for motor control.
the left hemisphere does not have an absolute dominance over the motor control of the right hand but that it does play a crucial role in mediating conceptual knowledge about the human body.
ideomotor apractic errors are due to a deficit in the translation of the concept of the human form into a motor plan.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the left hemisphere has a special role in the conceptual mediation of motor control.
the left hemisphere has a dominance for the control of the motor program for the imitation of meaningless gestures, but this dominance is not based on a motor dominance.
ideomotor apractic errors are not due to a failure of motor programming but rather to a failure to conceptualize the human body.
The main takeaway from our work is that
apractic errors in imitation are not necessarily due to a motor dominance of one hemisphere.
ideomotor apractic errors are not due to a motor deficit of the left hemisphere, but rather to a conceptual deficit.
the apraxic patient is not an ideal model of hemispheric specialization for motor control.
